checks.question: For each issued, nonvoid invoice outstanding on 2026-03-31, return its ID and positive balance in cents as of that date.
checks.sql:
SELECT i.id,
       SUM(l.amount_cents)
         - COALESCE((SELECT SUM(pa.amount_cents)
                     FROM payment_allocations pa
                     JOIN payments p ON p.id = pa.payment_id
                     WHERE pa.invoice_id = i.id
                       AND p.status = 'succeeded'
                       AND pa.allocated_on <= '2026-03-31'), 0)
         - COALESCE((SELECT SUM(ca.amount_cents)
                     FROM credit_applications ca
                     WHERE ca.invoice_id = i.id
                       AND ca.applied_on <= '2026-03-31'), 0) AS balance_cents
FROM invoices i
JOIN invoice_lines l ON l.invoice_id = i.id
WHERE i.status = 'issued' AND i.issued_on <= '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY i.id
HAVING balance_cents > 0
ORDER BY i.id;

         - COALESCE((SELECT SUM(ca.amount_cents)
                     FROM credit_applications ca
                     WHERE ca.invoice_id = i.id

checks.witness: Invoice 6 is status 'void' (lines 9000 cents) with credit application 1500 cents applied on 2026-03-16; dropping the status = 'issued' filter adds row [6, 7500] to the result. All other rows are identical, so this fixture fact isolates the void-exclusion assumption. Balances: inv1 6500-3000=3500 (alloc 8 on 2026-04-15 excluded), inv2 3000-1800-1000=200 (credit appl 2 on 2026-03-28), inv3 8000-3000-800=4200 (alloc 3 boundary 2026-03-31 included), inv4 2500 (alloc 4 on 2026-04-10 excluded), inv5 6000-2000-1000=3000 (alloc 6 on 2026-04-05 excluded, credit appl 4 boundary 2026-03-31 included), inv7 4500 (alloc 7 on 2026-04-05 excluded), inv8 1200 (credit appl 3 on 2026-04-05 excluded).

checks.question: Which payment IDs were successfully allocated to at least two distinct invoices by 2026-03-31?
checks.sql:
SELECT pa.payment_id
FROM payment_allocations pa
JOIN payments p ON p.id = pa.payment_id
WHERE p.status = 'succeeded' AND pa.allocated_on <= '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY pa.payment_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pa.invoice_id) >= 2
ORDER BY pa.payment_id;

ORDER BY pa.payment_id;
checks.witness: Payment 105 (succeeded, received 2026-04-05) was allocated to invoice 5 (3000 cents) and invoice 7 (1000 cents), both on 2026-04-05, which is after the 2026-03-31 cutoff; dropping the allocated_on cutoff adds row [105]. Payment 101 was allocated to invoices 1 and 2 on 2026-03-25 (within cutoff) and is the only correct answer. Failed payment 106 has no allocations, so it cannot mask this error.

checks.question: Return every customer ID and its total cents of credits applied to nonvoid invoices during March 2026, including zero.
checks.sql:
SELECT c.id AS customer_id,
       COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN i.status <> 'void' THEN ca.amount_cents END), 0) AS applied_cents
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN credit_applications ca
  ON ca.customer_id = c.id
 AND ca.applied_on BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-03-31'
LEFT JOIN invoices i
  ON i.id = ca.invoice_id
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY c.id;
checks.wrong_sql:
SELECT c.id AS customer_id,
       COALESCE(SUM(ca.amount_cents), 0) AS applied_cents
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN credit_applications ca
  ON ca.customer_id = c.id
 AND ca.applied_on BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY c.id;
checks.witness: credit_applications id=1 applies credit 201 for 1500 cents to invoice 6 (status 'void') on 2026-03-16 for customer 2; the gold SQL excludes applications to void invoices, so customer 2 totals 800 (application id=5 only), while the void-ignoring variant returns 2300. Application id=3 (700 cents, invoice 8) falls outside March 2026 (applied 2026-04-05), and customers 3 and 5 have no March applications, so the zero rows and the March cutoff are also exercised.

  ON il.invoice_id = i.id

Invoice 2 (subscription 1, 2026-03-20, one line), invoice 4 (subscription 3, 2026-03-25, one line) and invoice 6 (void, 2026-03-15, one line) are likewise excluded, while invoice 5 falls in February 2026; qualifying invoices are 1 (subscription 1, lines 5000+1500), 3 (subscription 2, lines 4000+4000) and 8 (subscription 3, lines 700+500).

checks.question: Return the three customers with the highest positive outstanding balances on 2026-03-31, as customer ID and balance in cents, descending by balance then ascending by ID.
checks.sql:
WITH totals AS (
  SELECT i.id AS invoice_id, i.customer_id, SUM(l.amount_cents) AS total_cents
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN invoice_lines l ON l.invoice_id = i.id
  WHERE i.status = 'issued' AND i.issued_on <= '2026-03-31'
  GROUP BY i.id, i.customer_id
),
alloc AS (
  SELECT pa.invoice_id, SUM(pa.amount_cents) AS cents
  FROM payment_allocations pa
  JOIN payments p ON p.id = pa.payment_id AND p.status = 'succeeded'
  WHERE pa.allocated_on <= '2026-03-31'
  GROUP BY pa.invoice_id
),
cred AS (
  SELECT ca.invoice_id, SUM(ca.amount_cents) AS cents
  FROM credit_applications ca
  WHERE ca.applied_on <= '2026-03-31'
  GROUP BY ca.invoice_id
)
SELECT b.customer_id, SUM(b.balance_cents) AS balance_cents
FROM (
  SELECT t.customer_id,
         t.total_cents - COALESCE(a.cents, 0) - COALESCE(c.cents, 0) AS balance_cents
  FROM totals t
  LEFT JOIN alloc a ON a.invoice_id = t.invoice_id
  LEFT JOIN cred c ON c.invoice_id = t.invoice_id
) b
GROUP BY b.customer_id
HAVING SUM(b.balance_cents) > 0
ORDER BY balance_cents DESC, b.customer_id ASC
LIMIT 3;

checks.question: Which nonvoid invoice IDs had a positive balance on 2026-03-31 and were fully settled by 2026-04-30?
checks.sql:
WITH totals AS (
  SELECT i.id AS invoice_id, SUM(l.amount_cents) AS total_cents
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN invoice_lines l ON l.invoice_id = i.id
  WHERE i.status = 'issued' AND i.issued_on <= '2026-03-31'
  GROUP BY i.id
),
alloc AS (
  SELECT pa.invoice_id,
         SUM(CASE WHEN pa.allocated_on <= '2026-03-31' THEN pa.amount_cents ELSE 0 END) AS by_0331,
         SUM(pa.amount_cents) AS by_0430
  FROM payment_allocations pa
  JOIN payments p ON p.id = pa.payment_id AND p.status = 'succeeded'
  WHERE pa.allocated_on <= '2026-04-30'
  GROUP BY pa.invoice_id
),
cred AS (
  SELECT ca.invoice_id,
         SUM(CASE WHEN ca.applied_on <= '2026-03-31' THEN ca.amount_cents ELSE 0 END) AS by_0331,
         SUM(ca.amount_cents) AS by_0430
  FROM credit_applications ca
  WHERE ca.applied_on <= '2026-04-30'
  GROUP BY ca.invoice_id
)
SELECT t.invoice_id
FROM totals t
LEFT JOIN alloc a ON a.invoice_id = t.invoice_id
LEFT JOIN cred c ON c.invoice_id = t.invoice_id
WHERE t.total_cents - COALESCE(a.by_0331, 0) - COALESCE(c.by_0331, 0) > 0
  AND t.total_cents - COALESCE(a.by_0430, 0) - COALESCE(c.by_0430, 0) = 0
ORDER BY t.invoice_id;
checks.wrong_sql:
WITH totals AS (
  SELECT i.id AS invoice_id, SUM(l.amount_cents) AS total_cents
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN invoice_lines l ON l.invoice_id = i.id
  WHERE i.status = 'issued' AND i.issued_on <= '2026-03-31'
  GROUP BY i.id
),
alloc AS (
  SELECT pa.invoice_id,
         SUM(CASE WHEN pa.allocated_on <= '2026-03-31' THEN pa.amount_cents ELSE 0 END) AS by_0331,
         SUM(pa.amount_cents) AS by_0430
  FROM payment_allocations pa
  JOIN payments p ON p.id = pa.payment_id AND p.status = 'succeeded'
  WHERE pa.allocated_on <= '2026-04-30'
  GROUP BY pa.invoice_id
)
SELECT t.invoice_id
FROM totals t
LEFT JOIN alloc a ON a.invoice_id = t.invoice_id
WHERE t.total_cents - COALESCE(a.by_0331, 0) > 0
  AND t.total_cents - COALESCE(a.by_0430, 0) = 0
ORDER BY t.invoice_id;
checks.witness: credit_applications.id = 4 (credit 204 -> invoice 5, 1000 cents applied 2026-03-31). Invoice 5 totals 6000 cents; succeeded allocations are 2000 (payment 104, 2026-03-15) + 3000 (payment 105, 2026-04-05) = 5000, so the invoice shows a positive 3000 balance on 2026-03-31 either way, but only the credit application brings it to exactly 0 by 2026-04-30; ignoring credits leaves 1000 outstanding and drops invoice 5 from the result.
